question.text: FSSAI standards are relevant to commodity derivatives because:

answer.text: They are a legal-risk input for commodities trading, while exchange contract specifications and SEBI/warehousing norms govern quality and good delivery
They have no connection to commodity markets

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists FSSAI standards as one source of legal risk for commodities trading. Commodity derivative contracts themselves specify quality/certification requirements, and SEBI/warehousing norms govern good delivery on the exchange side. The Trap: FSSAI does not regulate exchanges, set futures prices, or have zero connection to commodity markets. Note: The pages checked do not state that FSSAI standards themselves determine exchange delivery rejection or contract specifications, so the explanation stops at FSSAI being one legal-risk input rather than a direct delivery-rule source.
